QuestionStmt.S: Which of following on oxidation forms propanone?

Solution.S:
Propanone has the structure: CH₃COCH₃.

It is a ketone. Ketones are generally formed by oxidation of secondary alcohols.

Now, 2-propanol is: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃. Here, the —OH group is attached to the middle carbon, so it is a secondary alcohol. On oxidation, it gives propanone:

CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ + [O] → CH₃COCH₃ + H₂O

So, the correct option is: Option B: 2-Propanol.

Other options do not give propanone. 1-propanol is a primary alcohol, so it forms propanal or propanoic acid on oxidation. 2-butanol forms butanone. 2-methylbutan-1-ol is also a primary alcohol.
